sources.title: Micron Technology, Inc. XBRL company facts

evidence.text: Micron delivers a rich portfolio of high-performance DRAM, NAND, and NOR memory and storage products through our Micron® and Crucial® brands.
evidence.excerpt: Micron delivers a rich portfolio of high-performance DRAM, NAND, and NOR memory and storage products through our Micron® and Crucial® brands.

evidence.text: We continue to make significant investments to develop proprietary product and process technology, which generally increases bit density per wafer and reduces per-bit manufacturing costs of each generation of product.
evidence.excerpt: We continue to make significant investments to develop proprietary product and process technology, which generally increases bit density per wafer and reduces per-bit manufacturing costs of each generation of product.

evidence.text: We continue to introduce new generations of products that offer improved performance characteristics, including higher data transfer rates, advanced packaging solutions, lower power consumption, improved read/write reliability, and increased memory density.
evidence.excerpt: We continue to introduce new generations of products that offer improved performance characteristics, including higher data transfer rates, advanced packaging solutions, lower power consumption, improved read/write reliability, and increased memory density.

evidence.text: Our success is largely dependent on obtaining returns on our R&D investments, efficient utilization of our manufacturing infrastructure, development and integration of advanced product and process technologies, market acceptance of our diversified portfolio of semiconductor-based memory and storage solutions, and efficient capital spending.
evidence.excerpt: Our success is largely dependent on obtaining returns on our R&D investments, efficient utilization of our manufacturing infrastructure, development and integration of advanced product and process technologies, market acceptance of our diversified portfolio of semiconductor-based memory and storage

evidence.text: We face intense competition in the semiconductor memory and storage markets.
evidence.excerpt: We face intense competition in the semiconductor memory and storage markets.

evidence.text: The Cloud Memory Business Unit is focused on memory solutions for large hyperscale cloud customers, and HBM for all data center customers.
evidence.excerpt: •Cloud Memory Business Unit (“CMBU”): Focused on memory solutions for large hyperscale cloud customers, and HBM for all data center customers.

evidence.text: The Core Data Center Business Unit is focused on memory solutions for mid-tier cloud, enterprise, and OEM data center customers and storage solutions for all data center customers.
evidence.excerpt: •Core Data Center Business Unit (“CDBU”): Focused on memory solutions for mid-tier cloud, enterprise, and OEM data center customers and storage solutions for all data center customers.

evidence.text: The Mobile and Client Business Unit is focused on memory and storage solutions for the mobile and client segments.
evidence.excerpt: •Mobile and Client Business Unit (“MCBU”): Focused on memory and storage solutions for the mobile and client segments.

evidence.text: The Automotive and Embedded Business Unit is focused on memory and storage solutions for the automotive, industrial, and consumer segments.
evidence.excerpt: •Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (“AEBU”): Focused on memory and storage solutions for the automotive, industrial, and consumer segments.

evidence.text: The product portfolio includes memory and storage solutions, advanced solutions, and storage platforms based on high-performance semiconductor memory and storage technologies, including DRAM, NAND, and NOR.
evidence.excerpt: Our product portfolio of memory and storage solutions, advanced solutions, and storage platforms is based on our high-performance semiconductor memory and storage technologies, including DRAM, NAND, and NOR.

evidence.text: DRAM products are dynamic random access memory semiconductor devices with low latency that provide high-speed data retrieval with a variety of performance characteristics.
evidence.excerpt: DRAM: DRAM products are dynamic random access memory semiconductor devices with low latency that provide high-speed data retrieval with a variety of performance characteristics.

evidence.text: In 2025, the company began shipping the industry’s first 1γ (1-gamma) production node, which is the first DRAM node incorporating EUV lithography.
evidence.excerpt: In 2025, we began shipping the industry’s first 1γ (1-gamma) production node, which is our first DRAM node incorporating EUV lithography and offers further improvements in power efficiency, performance, and bit density compared to our prior DRAM node products.

evidence.text: The majority of the company's DRAM bit production in 2025 was on its leading-edge 1ß (1-beta) node.
evidence.excerpt: The majority of our DRAM bit production in 2025 was on our leading-edge 1ß (1-beta) node.

evidence.text: High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) utilizes through-silicon via (TSV) connections for more efficient communication, achieving a higher bandwidth while consuming less power compared to other memory types.
evidence.excerpt: High-Bandwidth Memory (“HBM”): A 3D stacked DRAM architecture that utilizes through-silicon via (“TSV”) connections for more efficient communication giving it the ability to achieve a higher bandwidth while consuming less power compared to other memory types.

evidence.text: DDR memory transfers data twice per clock cycle resulting in improved speeds, power efficiency, and storage density.
evidence.excerpt: Double Data Rate (“DDR”): DDR memory transfers data twice per clock cycle resulting in improved speeds, power efficiency, and storage density.

evidence.text: DDR5 is the fifth generation of DDR technology and offers critical improvements in bandwidth and power efficiency necessary to meet the growing needs of high-performance computing, AI, and data-intensive applications.
evidence.excerpt: DDR5 is the fifth generation of this technology and offers the critical improvements in bandwidth and power efficiency necessary to meet the growing needs of high-performance computing, AI, and data-intensive applications.

evidence.text: Low-Power DRAM (LPDDR) is engineered for mobile devices and applications requiring low power consumption.
evidence.excerpt: Low-Power DRAM (“LPDDR”): Engineered for mobile devices and applications requiring low power consumption.

evidence.text: LPDDR products generally operate at a lower voltage than standard DRAM products and are beneficial to any power conscious application.
evidence.excerpt: LPDDR products generally operate at a lower voltage than standard DRAM products and are beneficial to any power conscious application.

evidence.text: CMBU is focused on memory solutions for large hyperscale cloud customers, and HBM for all data center customers.
evidence.excerpt: CMBU is focused on memory solutions for large hyperscale cloud customers, and HBM for all data center customers.

evidence.text: CMBU sales to the data center end market are driven by server demand across the cloud market and includes our portfolio of HBM, high-capacity dual in-line memory modules (“DIMMs”), and low-power server DRAM solutions.
evidence.excerpt: CMBU sales to the data center end market are driven by server demand across the cloud market and includes our portfolio of HBM, high-capacity dual in-line memory modules (“DIMMs”), and low-power server DRAM solutions.

evidence.text: Overall cloud growth continues to be driven by the shift of both infrastructure and workloads from on-premises to the cloud.
evidence.excerpt: Overall cloud growth continues to be driven by the shift of both infrastructure and workloads from on-premises to the cloud.

evidence.text: Cloud-native workloads are driving growth through use cases such as AI-enabled intelligent edge devices and augmented reality platforms that store and access data in the cloud or rely on the cloud for compute capability.
evidence.excerpt: Cloud-native workloads are driving growth through use cases such as AI-enabled intelligent edge devices and augmented reality platforms that store and access data in the cloud or rely on the cloud for compute capability.

evidence.text: In 2024, we began volume production of our 8-high 24GB HBM3E with increased bandwidth and superior power efficiency enabled by our advanced 1β process node.
evidence.excerpt: In 2024, we began volume production of our 8-high 24GB HBM3E with increased bandwidth and superior power efficiency enabled by our advanced 1β process node.

evidence.text: In the fourth quarter of 2025, HBM3E 12-high represented the majority of our HBM shipments.
evidence.excerpt: In the fourth quarter of 2025, HBM3E 12-high represented the majority of our HBM shipments.

evidence.text: This enhanced version of HBM delivers faster data rates, improved thermal response, and a higher monolithic die density within the same package footprint as previous generations.
evidence.excerpt: This enhanced version of HBM delivers faster data rates, improved thermal response, and a higher monolithic die density within the same package footprint as previous generations.

evidence.text: In 2025, we delivered samples of HBM4 36GB 12-high to multiple key customers to power next-generation AI platforms.
evidence.excerpt: In 2025, we delivered samples of HBM4 36GB 12-high to multiple key customers to power next-generation AI platforms.

evidence.text: Our DDR5 alleviates this bottleneck by providing higher bandwidth than previous generations, enabling improved performance and scaling.
evidence.excerpt: Our DDR5 alleviates this bottleneck by providing higher bandwidth than previous generations, enabling improved performance and scaling.

evidence.text: In 2024, we qualified and began shipping our 128GB DDR5 server module, built on a monolithic 32GB DRAM die and powered by our 1ß node.
evidence.excerpt: In 2024, we qualified and began shipping our 128GB DDR5 server module, built on a monolithic 32GB DRAM die and powered by our 1ß node.

evidence.text: This innovative product provides an industry alternative to existing 3D TSV-based solutions to address the rigorous speed and capacity demands of memory-intensive generative AI applications.
evidence.excerpt: This innovative product provides an industry alternative to existing 3D TSV-based solutions to address the rigorous speed and capacity demands of memory-intensive generative AI applications.

evidence.text: In 2025, we began volume production of LPDDR5 in a small outline compression attached memory module (“SOCAMM”) form factor to enable easier server manufacturability and serviceability and to help drive broader LPDDR adoption in the server market.
evidence.excerpt: In 2025, we began volume production of LPDDR5 in a small outline compression attached memory module (“SOCAMM”) form factor to enable easier server manufacturability and serviceability and to help drive broader LPDDR adoption in the server market.

evidence.text: Total reported CMBU revenue was $13.52 billion in 2025, $3.79 billion in 2024, and $1.87 billion in 2023.
evidence.excerpt: Total reported CMBU revenue was $13.52 billion in 2025, $3.79 billion in 2024, and $1.87 billion in 2023.

evidence.text: CMBU sales to the data center market in 2025 consisted primarily of our HBM, DDR5 and DDR4, LPDDR5, and GDDR6 products.
evidence.excerpt: CMBU sales to the data center market in 2025 consisted primarily of our HBM, DDR5 and DDR4, LPDDR5, and GDDR6 products.

evidence.text: CDBU is focused on memory solutions for mid-tier cloud, enterprise, and OEM data center customers and storage solutions for all data center customers, including data center SSDs and NAND components.
evidence.excerpt: CDBU is focused on memory solutions for mid-tier cloud, enterprise, and OEM data center customers and storage solutions for all data center customers, including data center SSDs and NAND components.

evidence.text: CDBU sales to OEM data center customers are driven by server and storage demand to support mid-tier cloud and enterprise customers, and our sales consisted primarily of DDR5 and DDR4.
evidence.excerpt: CDBU sales to OEM data center customers are driven by server and storage demand to support mid-tier cloud and enterprise customers, and our sales consisted primarily of DDR5 and DDR4.

evidence.text: Our semiconductor memory and storage products are offered under our Micron and Crucial brand names and through private labels.
evidence.excerpt: Our semiconductor memory and storage products are offered under our Micron and Crucial brand names and through private labels.

evidence.text: We market our semiconductor memory and storage products primarily through our own direct sales force and maintain sales or representative offices to support our worldwide customer base.
evidence.excerpt: We market our semiconductor memory and storage products primarily through our own direct sales force and maintain sales or representative offices to support our worldwide customer base.

evidence.text: We sell our Crucial-branded products through a web-based customer-direct sales channel, as well as through channel and distribution partners.
evidence.excerpt: We sell our Crucial-branded products through a web-based customer-direct sales channel, as well as through channel and distribution partners.

evidence.text: In each of the last three years, approximately one-half of our total revenue was from our top ten customers.
evidence.excerpt: In each of the last three years, approximately one-half of our total revenue was from our top ten customers.

evidence.text: AI-driven demand is accelerating and is outpacing industry supply.
evidence.locator: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (Item 7), part 1/15
evidence.excerpt: AI-driven demand is accelerating and is outpacing industry supply.

evidence.text: In 2025, we benefited from substantial improvements in DRAM pricing, volumes and margins as compared to 2024.
evidence.locator: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (Item 7), part 1/15
evidence.excerpt: In 2025, we benefited from substantial improvements in DRAM pricing, volumes and margins as compared to 2024.

evidence.text: During 2025, we shifted a portion of our DRAM supply to the data center and hyperscale cloud markets to meet the strong demand fueled by AI.
evidence.locator: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (Item 7), part 1/15
evidence.excerpt: During 2025, we shifted a portion of our DRAM supply to the data center and hyperscale cloud markets to meet the strong demand fueled by AI.

evidence.text: The pivot to higher-growth segments, together with our strong execution, robust overall industry DRAM demand, and constrained supply, has led to improved profitability across our DRAM portfolio.
evidence.locator: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (Item 7), part 1/15
evidence.excerpt: The pivot to higher-growth segments, together with our strong execution, robust overall industry DRAM demand, and constrained supply, has led to improved profitability across our DRAM portfolio.

evidence.text: In 2025, NAND revenue increased from 2024 on higher bit shipments due to demand growth.
evidence.locator: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (Item 7), part 1/15
evidence.excerpt: In 2025, NAND revenue increased from 2024 on higher bit shipments due to demand growth.

evidence.text: The 2025 NAND gross margin percentage increased from 2024 due to cost reductions.
evidence.locator: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (Item 7), part 1/15
evidence.excerpt: The 2025 NAND gross margin percentage increased from 2024 due to cost reductions.

evidence.text: We continue to prudently manage our NAND business to ensure we align our supply growth and technology node cadence with our projections of the demand environment.
evidence.locator: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (Item 7), part 1/15
evidence.excerpt: We continue to prudently manage our NAND business to ensure we align our supply growth and technology node cadence with our projections of the demand environment.

evidence.text: Throughout 2024, we experienced substantial improvements in pricing and margins due to improving market conditions as compared to 2023.
evidence.locator: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (Item 7), part 1/15
evidence.excerpt: Throughout 2024, we experienced substantial improvements in pricing and margins due to improving market conditions as compared to 2023.

evidence.text: Increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI and mostly normal customer inventories, combined with industry-wide supply discipline, resulted in an industry supply and demand balance that substantially improved from downturn conditions in memory and storage markets during 2023.
evidence.locator: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (Item 7), part 1/15
evidence.excerpt: Increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI and mostly normal customer inventories, combined with industry-wide supply discipline, resulted in an industry supply and demand balance that substantially improved from downturn conditions in memory and storage markets during 2023.

evidence.text: In 2023, China’s Cyberspace Administration (the “CAC”) conducted a cybersecurity review of our products sold in China and decided that our products presented a cybersecurity risk.

evidence.excerpt: In 2023, China’s Cyberspace Administration (the “CAC”) conducted a cybersecurity review of our products sold in China and decided that our products presented a cybersecurity risk.

evidence.text: The CAC determined that critical information infrastructure operators in China may not purchase Micron products.

evidence.text: The CAC decision has impacted our business, particularly in the domestic data center and networking markets in China, and we have been working to mitigate that impact.
evidence.locator: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (Item 7), part 1/15
evidence.excerpt: The CAC decision has impacted our business, particularly in the domestic data center and networking markets in China, and we have been working to mitigate that impact.
